model.label: Social health insurance with a subsidised regime for the poor funded from general taxes and a contributory regime for formal workers, delivered through a public provider network (SNS) and private providers

overview.statement: The National Health Service (SNS) was created by Law 123-15 of 16 July 2015 as part of the country's health system reform.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

overview.statement: According to the SNS, its creation separated the functions of financing, regulation and service provision, in line with the General Health Law (Law 42-01) and the Dominican Social Security System law (Law 87-01).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

overview.statement: The 2018 World Bank study describes Law 87-01, approved by Congress in 2001, as establishing Family Health Insurance (SFS) with the goal of universality: protection for the entire population under one Basic Health Plan, with no exclusions.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

overview.statement: The SNS's 2025-2028 strategic plan says coverage under the Dominican Social Security System has grown steadily since 2001 and now reaches more than 98% of the population.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

overview.statement: In December 2024 the subsidised regime had 5,715,856 affiliates, according to the SNS plan's table of Social Security Treasury data.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

overview.statement: In December 2024 the contributory regime had 4,789,676 affiliates, according to the same table.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

financing.statement: The 2018 World Bank study says Family Health Insurance was designed to be financed from different sources: formal-sector employees (the contributory regime) through salary-based contributions by employee and employer, and the unemployed, disabled and people with income below the minimum wage by the government from general taxes.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

financing.statement: The 2018 World Bank study says the National Health Insurance (SENASA) was created as a public risk administrator to manage the subsidised regime and contract public providers.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

financing.statement: Spending financed by mandatory schemes (general taxes and social security contributions) rose from 1.8% of GDP in 2008 to 2.9% in 2015. Central government financing made up 62% of public health funds in 2008 and 55% in 2015.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

financing.statement: For the poor, supply-side financing (direct funding of providers) remained the major source: 86% in 2008 and 73% in 2015. Demand-side financing, assigned by SENASA through the subsidised regime (RS), rose from 14% to 27% over the same period.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

financing.statement: First-level care centres are paid by capitation to the Regional Health Services. About 20% of SENASA's transfers to them are meant for primary care, with a variable part tied to first-level care indicators.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

financing.statement: The SNS says health financing has historically concentrated on specialised levels of care, limiting the first level's ability to fulfil its role as a preventive, problem-solving gateway to the system.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

covered.statement: Law 87-01 provides for a Basic Health Plan covering health promotion and prevention, primary care including emergencies, specialised care and surgery, diagnostics, paediatric and preventive dental care, rehabilitation and complementary services. Outpatient medicines are covered at 100% for the subsidised population and 70% for the contributory and contributory-subsidised regimes.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

covered.statement: Negotiations in 2006 and 2007 over the content and cost of the Basic Health Plan led to a Health Services Plan (PDSS) based on negotiation rather than scientific evidence, according to the 2018 World Bank study.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

cost_sharing.statement: According to the 2018 World Bank study, power struggles over the Basic Health Plan delayed the contributory regime until a presidential decree mandated its start in September 2007. This resulted in reduced benefits, important copayments and financial ceilings on coverage, and the plan was renamed the Health Services Plan (PDSS).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

cost_sharing.statement: The 2018 World Bank study found that after the contributory regime began (2008 being the first year the reform's impact could be observed), public financing rose but not enough to change the overall financing structure or to significantly reduce out-of-pocket payments.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

cost_sharing.statement: PAHO's Health in the Americas profile reports for 2021 public expenditure on health of 3.29% of GDP and 17.74% of total public expenditure, with out-of-pocket spending at 23.59% of total health expenditure.

locator.section: Environmental and social determinants of health

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

access.statement: The SNS plan reports about 1.5 hospital beds per 1,000 inhabitants nationally (public and private), and about 0.8 per 1,000 in the public service network.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

access.statement: The SNS plan says marked inequalities in access persist, particularly in rural and border areas and vulnerable communities, where geographic dispersion and scarce health infrastructure in remote areas deepen barriers to timely care.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

access.statement: Public hospitals and primary care centres often become saturated as demand grows, and the SNS says many facilities operate in obsolete or inadequate physical conditions that harm quality and efficiency.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

access.statement: The SNS reports a critical shortage of medical, nursing and technical staff, especially in specialised areas and in rural and remote regions.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

access.statement: In 2024 the SNS employed 85,546 people. It had 22.09 health professionals per 10,000 inhabitants, below the international recommendation of at least 25 per 10,000.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

access.statement: Specialised health staff remain concentrated in the main urban areas, despite efforts to meet demand for specialists in rural and border regions.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

outcomes.statement: PAHO reports that in 2019 potentially avoidable premature mortality was 380 per 100,000, 67.6% above the regional average. Preventable-cause mortality was 219.8 per 100,000 (60.3% above the regional average) and treatable-cause mortality was 160.2, against a regional average of 89.6.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

outcomes.statement: The estimated maternal mortality ratio was 107.3 per 100,000 live births in 2020, 35.8% higher than the estimate for 2000.

locator.section: Health situation: Maternal and child health

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

outcomes.statement: Infant mortality fell from 39.1 to 22.7 deaths per 1,000 live births between 2000 and 2018, a 41.9% decrease.

locator.section: Health situation: Maternal and child health

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

outcomes.statement: The SNS plan says 2024 saw the most significant fall in infant and neonatal mortality rates, citing the national epidemiological surveillance system, with the neonatal rate down to 13.08 per 1,000 live births.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

outcomes.statement: A 2026 peer-reviewed paper says the country has made considerable progress on under-five mortality over past decades, but marked socioeconomic and geographic inequality persists, with children from poorer households and disadvantaged communities facing disproportionately higher risks.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

costs.statement: The SNS says the budget for the SNS and for the health sector as a whole remains limited relative to growing demand, which hampers maintenance, expansion, timely purchase of medicines and supplies, and key programmes.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

costs.statement: The SNS plan notes that the fall in inequality (the Gini index dropped 23.1 points between 2000 and 2023) has not yet fully translated into sufficient and sustainable health financing.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

costs.statement: Total health spending per head rose from US$506 in 2008 to US$814 in 2014 (PPP), and the World Bank described public per-capita spending as still low relative to other Latin American countries.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

what_works.statement: The 2018 World Bank study judged the reform successful in affiliating the population, separating functions, institutionalising mechanisms to collect and distribute funds, defining a comprehensive benefits package and protecting formal-sector workers financially.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

what_works.statement: Total affiliation to Family Health Insurance rose from 65,000 people in 2004 to 6.9 million in 2016, of whom 3.3 million were in the subsidised regime.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

what_works.statement: The World Bank study says the subsidised regime had practically covered everyone enrolled in the Unique System of Beneficiaries of Social Subsidies (SIUBEN).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

what_works.statement: A 2026 PAHO article reports that the country was among the first to join the Alliance for Primary Health Care in the Americas, an initiative launched in December 2023 by PAHO, the Inter-American Development Bank and the World Bank.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

problems.statement: The SNS says service delivery remains highly fragmented, with weak links between levels of care and between public and private providers, which limits continuity of care and causes duplicated procedures and delays.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

problems.statement: The SNS says coverage under the social security system has grown steadily, but that growth has not been matched by a proportional strengthening of the public network's capacity, leaving gaps in financing, case management and sustainability.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

problems.statement: The SNS says the public network faces high demand with limited resources and without equitable compensation for services given to affiliated people.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

problems.statement: PAHO quotes the SNS planning director as saying care in the Dominican Republic remains more hospital-based than preventive, with limited communication between levels and greater public trust in hospital services.

problems.statement: The 2018 World Bank study says the two regimes' accounts are kept separate even though revenue collection is centralised, so they are not pooled, which reduces solidarity and the possibilities of risk distribution.

problems.statement: The contributory-subsidised regime, designed in the 2001 law to cover informal-sector workers, was never implemented because of the difficulty of affiliating the informal sector.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

problems.statement: The SNS says the lack of a comprehensive, interoperable health information system prevents effective follow-up of patients across levels of care.

reforms.statement: In 2016 the government began steps to deepen the reform, aiming to affiliate 90% of the population by 2020. The function separation mandated by the 2001 law was implemented by unifying the public providers' network under a new entity separate from the Ministry of Health.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus (Opus subagent) support review (passage vs. statement)

reforms.statement: In December 2023 the World Bank approved a US$190 million project to strengthen the capacity to deliver quality health services in the Dominican Republic, particularly for poor and vulnerable people who depend most on the public system, with a further focus on maternal and neonatal care.
